v.rationale: I ranked impl-1 first, impl-2 second and impl-3 third. All three use the same architecture (invokable controller, FormRequest, an invokable BuildSalesReport action, #[Scope]/#[Fillable] attributes, enum cast, Number::currency) and all their suites pass: impl-1 25 tests, impl-2 22, impl-3 24. impl-1 is the most polished. It fetches aggregate rows with toBase(), qualifies its columns, echoes the applied filters and has the most thorough tests, covering rounding, thousands separators, status leakage and array input. Its probes (empty params, single-day range, an order with no items) all behaved correctly. impl-2 is equally correct and a little more compact, with configurable currency. It loses points for hydrating Order models to carry aggregate rows, for inlining every query into one long return array, and for an odd defensive tryFrom. impl-3 has a real contract bug: it uses 'sometimes' instead of 'nullable', so empty query params like `?status=` or `?from=` return 422 instead of falling back to the defaults (status paid). Probing confirmed this. It also repeats the filter scope chain right after defining a closure for it, uses unqualified scope columns, has a factory that queries the database for unit_price, and has small style lapses.
